newsitem.title: USA: U.S. again denies Colombia anti-drug certification.
newsitem.headline: U.S. again denies Colombia anti-drug certification.

text.p: The United States announced on Friday it was again denying Colombia certification as an ally in the fight against drugs.
It was the second consecutive year that Colombia was included on a list of states that had failed to cooperate fully in global anti-drug efforts.

"This year, like last year, the president's decision to deny certification to Colombia was the result of our concern that corruption remains rampant at the highest levels of the Colombian government, and that senior officials are failing to cooperate with us in the fight against drugs," Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said in announcing the decision.

The United States says that Colombia, under President Ernesto Samper, is a leading supplier of cocaine, a growing source of coca leaf -- the raw material for the drug -- and a leading supplier of heroin.

Washington charges that Samper not only accepted but solicited over $6 million from Colombian drug traffickers to finance his 1994 presidential campaign. Samper was absolved by the Colombian Congress last year of any wrongdoing in connection with his campaign finances.
